title: Static analysis run
description: A machine-checkable record of one static-analysis engine run (V2-36): the engine and its exact command, the rule set and its hash, the target commit, the raw engine output (SARIF), the normalized report and one triage entry per finding. A static-analysis finding is a review queue entry, not a verdict: it may be a true positive, a false positive, or a failure class no detector owns. The record therefore cannot support a `static-refinement` claim until every finding has a disposition: `covered` or `new` with a cell, detector and fixture that resolve; `not-a-bug` with a reason; or `out-of-scope` with a reason when the finding is real but the cited taxonomy does not own the failure class. L2 hashes the rule set and both outputs, ties `finished_at` to the evidence date, rejects an authored-fixture input and an unclassified finding (`unmapped`) for a non-open claim, and checks the triage bijection and routing. The record does not prove that the engine would have found a different defect; without an external anchor a forger can rewrite the record and its outputs together (C-13).

tool.description: Engine that produced the findings, e.g. 'semgrep', 'bandit', 'codeql', 'svace'. L2 checks it against an engine with at least one run in the normalized report.

version.description: Engine version. A rule set is interpreted by a version, so a version upgrade can change the answer.

command.description: Exact command that ran the engine, including the configuration, target and SARIF output. L1 requires it to equal the evidence command when the evidence names one.

rules.description: The rule set the engine applied. A finding is a function of the rules, not only of the code, so an unnamed or unhashed rule set makes the run unreproducible. A rule set fetched from a registry under a non-redistributable licence is named by URL: it is not vendored, and L2 does not fetch it.

name.description: Human name of the rule set, e.g. 'dev-sec-skills-ci-supply-chain'.

source.description: Path to the vendored rule file, relative to --tool-output-root, or the URL it was fetched from.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the rule bytes actually applied. L2 verifies it for a local path; a URL is not fetched and its hash is not re-derived.

target_commit.description: Commit of the analyzed repository. L1 requires it to equal the evidence commit when the evidence names one; L2 resolves it in --root when that root is a git work tree.

exit_code.description: Engine exit code. A non-zero code cannot support a non-open status; engines that return non-zero when findings exist need an adapter, not a reinterpretation of the code.

finished_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset. Its local date must equal the evidence date.

output.description: Path to the raw engine output (SARIF), relative to --tool-output-root, or a URL. A URL is not fetched and its hash is not checked, so L2 rejects it for a non-open claim.

output_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the raw output. L2 verifies it and that the normalized report hashes the same bytes as an input.

report.description: Path to the normalized report produced by tools/sarif_evidence.py, relative to --tool-output-root. The report, not the record, carries the finding identities the triage names. A URL is not fetched, the triage cannot be checked against it, and L2 rejects it for a non-open claim.

report_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the normalized report. L2 verifies it.

status.description: How the supervised run ended (V2-28 vocabulary). Only `completed` with exit_code 0 can support a non-open claim.

cells.description: Cell registry the triage's cell, detector and fixture fields resolve against, relative to --tool-output-root. Required when any entry has disposition covered or new.

triage.description: Exactly one entry per finding in the normalized report. An empty list is valid only when the report has no findings. `covered` and `new` name artifacts that must resolve; `not-a-bug` states why the finding is not a defect; `out-of-scope` states why a real finding has no owner in the cited taxonomy.

anchor.description: An SSH signature over the canonical bytes of the run (engine, command, rules hash, commit, both output hashes, exit code, timestamps, status and the whole triage list; see tools/anchor_subject.py). The signed subject, its signature and the allowed_signers file are committed and hashed here. L2 recomputes the canonical bytes and verifies the signature, so a record edited after signing stops verifying. The private key is not in the repository. The anchor does not stop the key holder, or anyone who can replace allowed_signers and re-sign: that is the remaining C-13 gap.

type.description: Signature scheme. Only ssh-ed25519 is implemented.

signer.description: Identity passed to `ssh-keygen -Y verify -I`; must appear in allowed_signers.

subject.description: Path to the signed canonical subject, relative to --tool-output-root.

allowed_signers.description: Path to the committed allowed_signers file that pins the public key.

finding.description: Finding id from the normalized report (`findings[].id`).

disposition.description: covered: an existing cell, detector and fixture already catch this failure class. new: no detector caught it, and the named cell, detector and fixture now exist. not-a-bug: the finding does not describe a defect, and the reason says why. out-of-scope: the finding describes a real symptom but the cited taxonomy owns no cell for its failure class; the reason names the boundary.

cell.description: Cell that owns the failure class. Required for covered and new.

detector.description: Detector of `cell` that catches the failure. Required for covered and new.

fixture.description: Mutation fixture in the `path#MUT-ID` form used by the cell registry. Required for covered and new.

reason.description: Why the finding is not a defect (not-a-bug) or why the taxonomy does not own it (out-of-scope). Required for both; the reason is the whole point of the entry.

note.description: Free-form context: observed output, fix, or follow-up.
